What are your favorite frugal gift ideas?
Grandma loved the ones I gave her last year!
I make soaps and put them in fancy glass jars tied with a pretty ribbon. One of my friends makes cookies and fudge and puts them in pretty metal containers. I love.hand made gifts.
I buy a lot of stuff second hand.

• Re-gifting of unwanted material goods

  • Self-made crap (cookies, beer, any hobby craft)

  • Dropping out of the whole holiday gift-exchange social ecosystem completely

The key to making a cheap, everyday item into an interesting gift is added value. Except you only have to do it at small scale, so it doesn't have to make much sense.

Food: You can flavor your own coffee. Pecan or chicory coffee is ubiquitous and expensive. Roast your own nuts, mix them with some moderately-priced beans, and you've got a special gift with your own flavor. You can make delicious candy like https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vmyogSgpASw and put it in fancy cellophane bags to make it look like the boutique stuff that sells for much money. Or get some of that wasabi pea seasoning and throw it on some dried vegetables or nuts.

Hardware: At pawn and thrift shops you can find used, full-of-character items at pawn shops like lighters, knives, and toolboxes which anybody could make use of with a little cleaning or paint. Hollow books aren't easy to do right, but they're great to receive, and as cheap as a hardback book at a thrift store and an exacto knife.

All these require taking time to test and shop, but they could work for anybody, even if they have no particular interest in coffee, toolboxes, or zippos.
